description: The Global Power Plant Database is an open database of power plants around the world, built by a collaboration of many partners coordinated by the World Resources Institute (WRI) and Google Earth Outreach. For each plant it records the name, primary and other fuel types, generation capacity, country, ownership, latitude and longitude, data source and URL, source year and annual generation, which is given at year scale for 2013 to 2017. Country data were read automatically from official government websites where possible, curated by hand elsewhere and matched to other databases such as the Global Energy Observatory and CARMA for geolocation. Coverage is worldwide at the level of individual plants. The latest release, version 1.3.0, is distributed as a CSV file through the WRI Data Explorer, which also offers a map layer and an API, and the build code is on GitHub; the data are licensed under CC-BY-4.0 at no cost. Caveats: WRI states that the project is no longer maintained and that no updates are planned since early 2022; generation years may be calendar, fiscal or regulatory years without distinction, and the order of the other-fuel columns carries no meaning. Simulation uses are capacity planning, exposure of generation assets to hazards and building supply nodes for network models. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
